meaningMnemonic: This radical is the same as the kanji. It means attach .

See the samurai on top of the giant bean? He's standing over it and using it as a drum . Back in the day, samurai used drums to communicate and amp themselves up in battle, and when things were desperate, any ol' giant bean would do. Can you imagine a samurai drumming out a war beat on a giant bean drum?

This is the face radical, because it looks kind of like a face. See the flat brow on top? Imagine some eyes under it, a blocky nose in the middle, and some big ol’ cheeks on either side. It's a little bit square, but that's just what a face looks like when you take away the head and you're left with nothing but a face.
This radical is the same as the kanji. It means valley .
This radical has a figure reaching out both hands at you with some dirt on his head. This is a zombie , and he must have just recently dug himself out of the grave by the looks of it.

A tsunami hits a valley , filling it up with water. Lucky for you, you're a giant, so you just lay down in the valley and use it to bathe . Hints Sure, there's a lot of water in the valley, but you're big too. It's the perfect place for you to bathe... and good thing too, you're getting smelly.
readingMnemonic: You know what would make the bath ing experience even better? If you had some egg yolk s ( よく ) to eat. Just crack those yolks into the water you bathe in, and it'll cook to perfection. Yum! Hints Imagine cooking egg yolks in the same water you bathe in.

meaningMnemonic: With the bamboo from that tree , your trained eye can tell it'll make an excellent box . Boxes made from bamboo trees are very sturdy and fashionable. You have an eye for fashion as well, you see. Hints Remember back to those woodshop electives you had in school (if you did have them) and imagine yourself crafting a bamboo box out of a bamboo tree you felled yourself. Don't forget to wear eye protection though! Wouldn't want anything to happen to those valuable eyes of yours.
readingMnemonic: Now you can use that box to store all your ha rd co re ( はこ ) punk vinyl records. You're a real connoisseur, so you know that hardcore music should only ever be kept in bamboo boxes. Hints Picture yourself filling up your lovingly crafted bamboo box with your collection of hardcore punk and rock records. Ah, they fit just perfectly thanks to that discerning eye of yours.

meaningMnemonic: A psychic leader kneels to the ground , picks up a thread , and instantly makes a connection with the person that it came from. This leader is very powerful, so even a thread is enough for them to make a psychic connection with the person who was wearing it. Hints Imagine you're this leader, and you've just picked up a piece of thread from the ground. You make a jarring psychic connection with the owner of the thread. Your head spins, your heart races, and your hands tremble. Picture this happening to you as you pick up the thread from the ground.
readingMnemonic: As you develop this psychic connection with the owner of the thread, you can tell that they're currently eating a ca ke ( けい ). Hints The connection is so strong that you feel like you're eating the cake as well. It's vanilla-strawberry. You taste the fluffy and creamy vanilla-strawberry flavors washing over your tongue. Imagine yourself eating this delectable cake. It's fantastically delicious.

meaningMnemonic: After a tsunami , use this machine to cure the people and the country from the damage. Heal ing machines are all over Japan just in case a tsunami does way more damage than they can handle. Oh, and whoever cures and heals the most people will be able to rule over them once everything starts going back to normal. So keep that in mind, kay? Hints Imagine if you had your own machine to cure yourself if a tsunami came to where you live. It would be pretty convenient!
readingMnemonic: Alternative ways to cure yourself after a tsunami are either praying to Je sus ( じ ) or eating your weight in chee se ( ち ). I'm not sure if I have enough cheese for all the people that got hit though... Hmm, do you have cheese? Before you make your decision, remember that whoever cures you will be able to reign over you and your people. So do you want to be led by Jesus or by some cheese? The choice is yours. Hints Imagine getting Jesus to cure half the people and feeding the other half lots of cheese and their wounds miraculously healing on their own! You're a hero!

meaningMnemonic: There is a prison on a cliff surrounded by snake s. Now that's a dangerous place. If you try to escape the prison you either fall to your death off the cliff or get bitten/squeezed to death by the snakes. Can you think of anything more dangerous than this? I can't. Hints Imagine a dangerous prison surrounded by cliffs and snakes. You wouldn't want to be here either, would you?
readingMnemonic: Lucky for you, even though you're stuck in this dangerous place, there is hope. There is a key ( き ). All dangerous prisons have a key. You just have to find and steal it so you can avoid the cliffs and snakes! Hints Imagine staring at the key dangling right outside of the dangerous prison you're trapped in. Would you take the chance and go for it?

meaningMnemonic: When the sun gets in your eye , I dare you to stare at it. I dare you to look right at the sun. I dare you. Hints Looking at the sun straight on hurts. It’s bad for your eyes and burns your brain. Imagine how painful it is to stare at the sun.
readingMnemonic: After you’ve blinded yourself from the dare of looking at the sun and losing sight in each eye, the guy dares you to go bow ling ( ぼう ). You’re blind now, so bowling will be quite the challenge. Hints Picture yourself bowling without the power of sight. It would be awfully difficult to do well. You’d just have to concentrate really hard on the sound of the pins and determine where you need to throw the ball.

meaningMnemonic: You can observe how the sun casts shadows behind two Wolverine s and a turkey to figure out the day of the week . Outside of a calendar, it's the best way to figure out what day it is. Hints The two Wolverine shadows are like clock hands, and the turkey's tail fan is like a clock face or something… Man, I don't know. Just trust me on this "day of the week" hack.
readingMnemonic: Now that you know how to figure out what day of the week it is, you can start making yo gurt ( よう ). It can take up to 24 hours to make yogurt. Knowing which day of the week it is at any given moment means you can perfect your yogurt-making schedule. Hints Picture yourself looking at the shadow cast by the two Wolverines and the turkey. Imagine waiting a whole 24 hours and knowing exactly when your yogurt is ready. All thanks to this makeshift sundial which can accurately tell you which day of the week it is.

meaningMnemonic: A group of private sword guys are in your rice paddy . You must detain them at once! Private sword guys are people who work for private companies and use their swords on people. They're basically paid assassins. And you're going to detain them! Hints Imagine running into the rice paddy and detaining the private sword holders one by one. They won't get away this time!
readingMnemonic: You're running out of steam and you're afraid you might not be able to detain all of these guys when Ryu ( りゅう ) from Street Fighter appears. He hates swords, and will only use fists because it's the honorable way to fight, so he starts helping you detain them! He's also found a loo phole ( る ) in the system and you don't have to be super gentle with these guys either. So detain them as forcefully as you want. It is your rice paddy they're in, after all. Hints If Ryu hadn't shown up with this loophole you never would have detained all these private sword guys by yourself!

meaningMnemonic: If you listened in to the private lives of twenty people, all of them would have different dialect s and ways of speech . Whether they actually use these dialects with you is another story. But when they're alone, or with other people who are from the same place, their speech will be different. Hints Can you even imagine twenty different dialects in your head? Well I can tell you that there are definitely at least twenty of them in Japan alone.
readingMnemonic: The best way to learn someone's dialect is to buy them a ben to ( べん ) from where they're from. Not only do these bento have writing in their dialect on them, but their speech will immediately shift to match. Then you'll be able to hear how they sound in their head and in private! Hints It also helps that bento are delicious, and anyone with any dialect will love them.

meaningMnemonic: What I say is correct 100%! You may use it as evidence in this murder case. Hints You convince the officials questioning you that your evidence can be trusted and it's proof that you definitely didn't have anything to do with any law breaking or murdering.
readingMnemonic: The officials force you to present this evidence in front of the Shou gun ( しょう ), himself. Your knees quake, you feel like you're gonna be sick, but you try to stand up tall and tell him everything. After all, you know your proof is correct, so you shouldn't be so scared. Hints You better hope the Shougun believes your evidence is accurate, because he's known to kill people willy-nilly when he thinks they're lying.

meaningMnemonic: If a narwhal stick s a child with its horn then you have to admit that it exist s. We know some of you have been doubting narwhals and whether they're real. Well now your kid is a kabob, so do you believe they exist now? I suppose you do. Hints Imagine needing this kind of horrible proof to believe something exists. Maybe you should have more faith in what we teach.
readingMnemonic: Oh, and the child we had to narwhal stab to prove they exist - that's your son ( そん ). Maybe you should have listened and kept your son out of the Narwhal Danger Zone ( ぞん ) after we warned you about it. Hints I suppose you'll never forget that narwhals exist now that your son has one permanently stuck in him.

meaningMnemonic: The face radical and the face kanji are the same! But this isn't just a face like the one you're looking at your computer/phone with. It's the surface kind of face too! Hints The next time you look at your face, also notice how much surface area it has.
readingMnemonic: This face you're looking at, that has a lot of surface area, belongs to men ( めん ). Not a single man, but all men put together. It's hundreds of thousands of men's faces in a row. Hints Look at the face of all men put together. Measure how much surface area they all take up.

meaningMnemonic: You see a scooter with a zombie on it, going really far away. Someone tied that zombie to the scooter and now it's far off in the distance, groaning and growling. Hints Picture the zombie, going far off into the distance. It's getting smaller and harder to see.
readingMnemonic: The zombie goes so far , that its life en ds ( えん ). Zombies need to eat to live (it's really all they need), but they go so far on their scooter trip, that they just give up and end it all. Hints I mean, to be fair, the zombie wasn't really alive to begin with. But going far enough to end it all? That's some serious distance!

meaningMnemonic: You examine the mouth of a zombie and find a small garden in there. There are even benches... it looks like a park . Hints Zombies are dead, so I guess their mouths have all the things garden plants crave. Their mouths are like compost piles, if you think about it.
readingMnemonic: You look closer at the garden and suddenly everything en ds ( えん ). Hints Oh. The zombie probably bit down on your head and now it's the end for you. At least you were looking at a nice garden at the end of it all...

meaningMnemonic: The radical for gate and the kanji for gates are the same! Hints Know your radicals or you won't be allowed to pass.
readingMnemonic: You want to pass through this gate but it’s guarded by… a mon ster ( もん )! Hints Picture the most terrifying monster you can imagine, standing as tall as the gate itself. How on earth are you ever going to get past that thing?!

meaningMnemonic: A canopy attach ing your entire country is the government . They loom over you all and try to keep you all organized and together under their control. Hints Picture a map of the world with actual canopies attached to each government, representing the ruling governments of each place.
readingMnemonic: Try to get out from under this government canopy and you'll be labeled a foo l ( ふ ). Unless... you can fool them! Hints Think of all the people who've been labeled as fools by the government because they try to detach themselves from under their reach. It's a pretty long list...

meaningMnemonic: Put a lid on something spicy and you'll cook up pure happiness . Hints Spicy foods literally do trigger happy chemicals in your brain. It wouldn't be too far off to say that putting a lid on a pot filled with something spicy could produce happiness.
readingMnemonic: Out of spicy foods you made pure happiness . You give it to your sad friend こう いち , who waits at the table. Hints こういち looks sad. But when you serve him happiness, he starts to perk up a bit. A couple more bites of happiness, and there's a smile on his face. Although when you found こういち he was depressed, down on his luck, and hiding from the government, cooking him some spicy foods seems to have brought him some happiness.

meaningMnemonic: In the prison where you once kept Wolverine , you find a beating heart . You don't understand how it's still going, but you know you need to hurry up and do something, or it might stop all of a sudden . Hints Picture this beating heart in the prison. Was it Wolverine's? That would explain why it's, like, beating all supernaturally on its own. What should you do with it? You'd better hurry, its owner probably needs it.
readingMnemonic: You start to overheat as you hurry around, so you grab a cu cumber ( きゅう ) to cool you down. The high water content re-hydrates you and lets you continue hurrying to help save this heart. Hints And if it really is Wolverine's heart, you're gonna have to be cool as a cucumber when you try to help him, even if you're in a hurry. He's emotionally cold, remember? Gotta play it cool with him, despite the emergency.

meaningMnemonic: Bamboo heaven is a place for laugh ing. Bamboo is a very jolly plant, and they love to laugh. Even after death in bamboo heaven, the bamboo continue to laugh joyfully. Bamboo heaven is truly a place of laughter. Hints Imagine yourself as a bamboo plant that laughs in heaven. What are you laughing about? Chuckle to yourself as you remember this kanji.
readingMnemonic: There’s actually a war a goin’ on up in that there bamboo heaven, y’know? Ye might not have heard of it with all that there laugh in’ a goin’ on, but there definitely be a war a ( わら ) goin’ on up in bamboo heaven, y’hear? The bamboo are scared so that’s why they be laughin’ so much. They nervous. Hints Now picture these bamboo again up in bamboo heaven, and remember this strange accent to remember that the bamboo plants up in bamboo heaven are laughing with nervous laughter at this bamboo war that’s a goin’ on up there.

meaningMnemonic: You offer flowers to your leader and compliment them on their lip ring . You think that by doing this they might carry your luggage . Hints Picture this big, strong leader. They actually love flowers and feel flattered by your compliment! But being the leader, they can't help wondering why they should have to carry your luggage…
readingMnemonic: Unconvinced by your flattery, the leader refuses to carry your luggage , so you get on your knee s ( に ) and beg them to carry it. Hints On top of being a strong leader, they also have a very kind heart, so your begging convinces them and they agree to carry your luggage.

meaningMnemonic: The place that buildings feel very anti - towards is Osaka . Osaka is the last place they want to be built. Why? Because chances are they'll be built on a slope . Osaka has a lot of big slopes, and buildings hate being built on slopes. Hints Try to imagine standing your whole life on a big, slanted slope, like one of these buildings that are so anti-Osaka. Wouldn't be easy, would it? By the way, although this kanji literally means "slope," it's mainly just used in the name for Osaka and to refer to the Osaka region, so that's the meaning we'll focus on.
readingMnemonic: Who lives in Osaka at the top of a big slope ? It's Han ( はん ) Solo. Hints Han loves Osaka for its gritty, port-city vibe, which reminds him of the spaceport cantinas he used to frequent. And he chooses to live on top of a slope because he wants to be closer to space… obviously.

meaningMnemonic: The hat comes to a stop , thinking of a plan . The hat had been pacing around for a while, trying to think of how to get off the head he's resting upon and back into the house where it's nice and cozy, and came to the sudden realization of a plan. This caused the hat to stop. Hints Imagine a hat walking about on your head, pacing back and forth deep in thought. See the hat stroke its chin in contemplation as it tries to think up a plan to get off your noggin and back inside.
readingMnemonic: The plan that made this hat stop right in its tracks was very simple. First, obtain the key ( き ) to the house. Then, use the key to get in the front door. How simple! Hints Watch as the hat begins to grin. This plan is so simple it’s sure to work. Now watch as the hat obtains the key and enters the locked door. What sort of mischief will the hat get into once inside?

meaningMnemonic: It's correct in winter to focus on politics and the government . Elections are happening, in the new year politicians are being sworn in. Winter is government time! Hints Imagine all this politics and government talk as you shiver outside in the winter cold. You’re freezing and you’re bored, but you know this is the right (correct) thing to do.
readingMnemonic: Everyone involved in politics and government wields a special sa ber ( せい ). If two political parties are arguing, they'll whip out their sabers and start slashing away! Hints Picture two different politicians, both wielding sabers, fighting to make the government the way they want it to be! Who are you rooting for?

meaningMnemonic: The kanji is the same as the products radical, so it means product — you know, the kind of article s or goods you buy and sell. Hints Which store has the best product selection, do you think? Picture all those articles and goods lined up on the shelves in their little boxes, kind of in the shape of this kanji.
readingMnemonic: As you try to sell some product s, you finally get a buyer. It's a Hin du ( ひん ) person. She walks in and buys your products on the spot! Hints Then another Hindu person walks in your store and buys some. Then another... What are all these Hindu people doing buying your products, you wonder? When you ask them, they tell you "it's a cultural thing."

meaningMnemonic: Your roof needs measurement s done every year to make sure it will protect you properly. Hints If you think about it, your roof protects you from a lot of things! Rain, snow, bird poop. But if your roof's measurements are off it won't be able to protect you properly.
readingMnemonic: If the measurements are off, and your roof doesn't protect you, then you get to sue ( す )! If you're still alive, that is. Hints Odds are, the roof collapsed or a tree fell on you and you died from lack of protection. So now your family and friends are going to sue on your behalf.

meaningMnemonic: When your tongue becomes too spicy for you to bear, it’s time to quit the jalapeño eating contest. You’ve been eating them for three hours now and the spiciness from the peppers is really burning your tongue. Throw in the towel, it’s time to quit the contest. This kanji has another meaning too: Eating isn't the only thing that makes your tongue spicy , so do certain word s. Say your favorite words out loud right now. Feel them on your tongue. Words are the spicy food of language! Hints You may have to quit eating but you never have to quit saying words. Especially if you're, well, trying to learn a whole new language full of them.
readingMnemonic: Oh, you're probably wondering who won that spicy food contest after you quit and became obsessed with word s instead. It was Je sus ( じ ). Who did you expect? He was great with words AND never quitting when things got spicy. Hints Picture Jesus scarfing down jalapeño peppers. He never quits. And then he says some words about how the jalapeños gave up their lives for this contest, so we better appreciate them. Thanks Jesus!

meaningMnemonic: If the pope stays fixated on the ground , staring at fins , he's going to lose touch with reality . He should be focusing on his popish duties, but instead he's looking at the fish fins he dropped, and now can't eat because they're dirty. Silly pope. You can't let this one thing get you down. You have other things to do. Hints Picture trying to get the pope to stop staring at the fins lying on the dirty ground. Yup, he's completely lost touch with reality, you think.
readingMnemonic: You're doing your best to bring the pope back to reality when he snaps and kicks you in the shin ( しん ). Oww! What the heck, pope! But he's already back staring at the fins and your shin is throbbing where he kicked it. Hints Imagine the pope angrily kicking your shin super hard. You fall over and pull it close. Feel how badly it aches. Who knew you'd need shin guards to deal with a pope that's lost touch with reality just from dropping his dinner.

meaningMnemonic: This gate of horns will take you to heaven . These horns are related and connected to heaven in some way. Hints Perhaps they are related to heaven because the devil has horns? Perhaps they are connected to heaven because these are the horns of heaven's enemies? The real reason they're connected will be revealed in the reading mnemonic.
readingMnemonic: They are related and connected to heaven because these are the horns that Genghis Khan ( かん ) made from his enemies. God said he could come into heaven if he made a gate of horns, so that's what he did. Hints Imagine Genghis Khan taking horns off his enemies, and making a gate to heaven. The horn gate is connected to both heaven and Genghis Khan in that way.

meaningMnemonic: Going into a building made by a squid is risky . First of all, squids only have tentacles, no bones, and they make all of their buildings out of risky materials like kelp and sharp coral. Hints One squid got stuck in his own building, but no one could save him because going in would be too risky. Poor little squid.
readingMnemonic: "It's too risky , leave me!" the squid cries. "I'll save you, underwater citizen! Nothing is too risky for Ken ( けん ) the samurai!" The building is collapsing on the squid, the risk is so great, but Ken the samurai dives in and saves him! Hints The squid cries, "I can build one that isn't so risky next time!" Ken shakes his head, "I'm not letting you do anymore risky things, you're coming with me from now on." Ken scoops up the squid into a bucket, hoists him over his shoulder, and walks off into the sunset. Who knows what adventures await our new duo. All we know is that they'll definitely be getting into some risky business.

meaningMnemonic: If you play music with your fins , one rule is that you must be a fish. You can’t play music using fish fins that don’t belong to you. That’s the rule. And it’s also rude. Hints Imagine a fish playing music using his fins. What kind of a song is it? Imagine it in your head as you see a sign with the fish fin rule on it.
readingMnemonic: There’s also a rule in place to limit the amount of fish fin musicians. No more than ten ( てん ) are allowed to gather and play their music together. That’s the rule. No more than ten. Hints Picture a group of ten (as per the rule) fish playing music with their fins. Now the song can be louder and more intricate. Imagine it playing in your head.

meaningMnemonic: Sticking a cross into a rice paddy to get its measurement s is your specialty . Most people get really confused when they have to measure their rice paddies, but that's where you come in. You plant a cross right in the middle, look down it from one end to the other, and voila! You know the measurements immediately. That's why it's your specialty! Hints Visualize yourself doing this. The numbers just come to you. It's just what you're good at. Your specialty is something no one else in the world is as good at as you!
readingMnemonic: Hearing of your amazing specialty and cross measurement abilities, a cen taur ( せん ) from a far off land recruits you for a job. The centaur’s father has just passed away and the centaur wants you to measure the rice paddies that have been left to him. Hints Picture yourself at a centaur funeral. Tons of centaurs standing around and stamping their hooves as you make your measurement and stick a cross into the ground.

meaningMnemonic: A forehead table is completely superfluous . Hints Seriously, you don't need a forehead table. It's totally unnecessary to have a table made of foreheads and is a superfluous purchase. First of all, getting all those foreheads is a waste of people. Second, forehead tables aren't very strong. Superfluous, superfluous, superfluous.
readingMnemonic: The only person you know with a superfluous forehead table is Joe ( じょう ), the ten foot tall, simple farmhand. Hints Now every time you visit Joe, you’ll have to look at his giant, superfluous forehead table. Imagine how gross it looks, with dozens of foreheads protruding from its surface. Only Joe would buy such a thing.

meaningMnemonic: Why would you try to take a brush to the sun ? It's almost too obvious, because you want to write something down. Hints Just imagine yourself sitting on the sun, writing back to your friends and family with a brush. For someone who can visit the sun, it's really weird that you are writing with a brush like this, but you're doing it just the same.
readingMnemonic: What did you write about? You were writing about this amazing circus show ( しょ ) you just watched on the sun. You didn't expect there to be any shows here, but turns out you were wrong! Hints Think of your favorite live shows and imagine them on the sun. Also imagine yourself writing back to your friends and family about said shows.

meaningMnemonic: You have gotten a mission. You must go out and detain a dangerous criminal to protect your country. While you go do that, you will be away from home and have an absence from society.
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

to visit while someone is away
to keep watch while someone is away
to take charge during someone's absence

sentences.english: I visited Koichi's house, but he was not there.

僕の彼女は料理人としてレストランで働いています。

sentences.english: Chefs also need to pay attention to the presentation of their dishes.

meaningMnemonic: If you are able to enter the gate then you have gained admission and entrance to the facility.  Sometimes you do this to start an apprenticeship , where you get an introduction to some sweet new skills, like how to make an entrance.
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

to decide to become an apprentice

sentences.english: Let's start with the introductory course first.

sentences.english: I heard he started his training under a famous yoga instructor.

sentences.english: This book is an introductory text on programming.

meaningMnemonic: You dare to do something risky . It's adventure time! Imagine yourself daring yourself to do risky things. Is this an adventure? If not, make it so!
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

sentences.english: to set off on an adventure
to go out on an adventure

sentences.english: We should reserve our energy for our adventure tomorrow.

sentences.english: Wow, this illustration gives off the vibe of an adventurer's tavern, huh?

sentences.english: Koichi left his job at WaniKani and embarked on a new adventure with Pikachu.

meaningMnemonic: You should write down all your thoughts on this day , because it's not just any day — it's an anniversary ! Wondering how 記念日 differs from 周年 ? 周年 is usually for a numbered anniversary, like 十周年 (10th anniversary), whereas 記念日 refers to the specific date on which a memorable event took place in the past.
readingMnemonic: The reading is a combination of on'yomi for the first two and kun'yomi for the last one. That being said, all of the readings for all of the kanji are the readings you've learned already, so you should be able to read this word too. Just watch out because ひ is rendaku'd into び .

sentences.english: to make into a holiday, to make into a commemorative day
to become a holiday, to become a commemorative day
to go out on one's anniversary, to go out on a commemorative day

sentences.english: I'm planning to go to dinner with him on our anniversary.

sentences.japanese: 今は『サラダ記念日』を読んでいます。
今日は『ワニカニ様』の放送開始記念日です。
sentences.english: Today is the anniversary of the broadcast debut of "WaniKani-sama."

meaningMnemonic: Someone has the status of being like d by you, and it's because of their incredible appearance and form . They have a great look , and it's really making you like them (you're kind of superficial). On its own, 格好 usually refers to how someone comes across visually, especially their clothing or outward style. Just be sure to note the かく reading, which gets changed to かっ . Note that in casual speech, people often shorten 格好 's reading from かっこう to かっこ . This is especially common with the phrases 格好いい and 格好悪い , which tend to be shortened to かっこいい and かっこわるい — and even written that way in kana sometimes. BUT… when it's time for kanji exams, remember to use the official reading かっこう for 格好 !

meaningMnemonic: The outside face of something is its external appearance . 外面 usually refers to someone's outward demeanor or behavior, especially when it's considered inauthentic somehow. In other situations, this word can also just mean the literal surface of something.
readingMnemonic: This word has two readings, そとづら and がいめん . We'll focus on the more common そとづら one here. But you didn't learn the つら reading with 面 , and it gets rendaku'd in this word, so here's a mnemonic: Your external appearance is always perfect because before meeting anyone, you put on a du-ra g ( づら ). The du-rag magically makes you seem kind and friendly, even when you're not. It's just a part of your outward demeanor , or そとづら . Reminder: The そとづら reading usually implies a kind of deceptive outward demeanor. For a neutral word for surfaces or external appearances, like the exterior of a building, use がいめん .

meaningMnemonic: In history , there are people who rise above others to be the first to do something. That makes them the first in history . 史上初 is used for any historic first . First human on the moon, first photograph ever taken, first movie to gross a billion dollars — that kind of thing.

meaningMnemonic: The kanji and the word are exactly the same, so this means inside or within . While 中 refers to the inside of something in a basic, positional sense, 内 tends to express a more abstract version of "inside," like 心の内を話す (express your inner feelings) or 温かい内に飲む (drink it while it's still warm). It also carries an implied contrast with 外 (outside), so it's often used to talk about yourself or your group, like うちの犬 (our dog) or うちの会社 (the company I work for). In this case, it's almost always written in hiragana as うち — which is why we used it like that in these examples (but hey, now you know where that うち is coming from!).
readingMnemonic: Since this word is made up of a single kanji, it should use the kun'yomi reading. When learning the kanji, you didn't learn that reading, so here's a mnemonic to help you with this word: If someone were to peek inside your heart, they would say, " Ooh, chee se ( うち )!" Most people's hearts are full of emotions and crippling insecurities and stuff, but yours has nothing but cheese within it. "Ooh, cheese… I love you so." That's all your heart's inner voice is ever saying.

meaningMnemonic: Remember how 問う means "to question something" and 合わせる means "to join together"? If you're joining your questions together, you're probably trying to to inquire about something. Inquiring is much more involved than plain old asking, after all. 問い合わせる is a phrase you can use when contacting a business or government office to request information or resolve an issue. It's a bit formal, but in an everyday business-speak kind of way, and it doesn't have the philosophical or weighty tone that 問う does.
readingMnemonic: You probably know how to read 問う and 合わせる already. 問う is still pretty new though, so here's a mnemonic to help you remember the 問 part: You love to inquire with your toe s ( と ). Whenever you fill out one of those online forms to contact customer support with an inquiry, you do all your typing with your toes. They don't know you're making this inquiry with your toes — but you do, and it makes you chuckle.

meaningMnemonic: This word is a combination of 付く (to be attached) and 合う (to suit). You and another person almost seem to be attached at the hip because you suit each other so well, and maybe that's why you chose to keep company with each other in the first place. 付き合う is a versatile word for spending time or going along with someone. It's often romantic, like 彼と付き合っている (I'm dating him), but it can be totally neutral too, like 仕事仲間と付き合う (hang out with work friends). From this, it can also extend to negative situations, like わがままに付き合う (put up with someone's selfishness) or 病気と付き合う (live with an illness). You're "keeping company" with this thing over time — even when it's inconvenient or difficult.
readingMnemonic: The reading comes from 付く and 合う , so if you remember those, you should be fine here.

meaningMnemonic: This word consists of kanji with hiragana attached. Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means hard so the verb vocab version? sentences.japanese: 多くのコアラはコアラレトロウィルスというウイルスを先天的に保持しており、ストレスなどを受けると、死につながることがあります。ですので、動物園では、カメラのフラッシュや大声を出すなどしないよう、十分気をつけてください。
